# Pertemuan 6: Simulasi Monte Carlo

## 2. Simulasi Monte Carlo Standar: *Direct Sampling*

### 2.1. Kasus Estimasi Nilai $\pi$ berdasarkan Bola Homogen

Metode *acceptance-rejection* digunakan untuk mengestimasi nilai $\pi$ dengan pendekatan bola homogen dengan jari-jari $2R$ pada ruang kubus dengan panjang sisi $2R$.

Fungsi:

```{r}
# Estimasi nilai π dengan metode acceptance-rejection
estimate_pi <- function(n_points, R = 1) {
  ### Fungsi ini mengestimasi nilai π dengan metode acceptance-rejection ###
  ### Input:
  ### n_points = banyaknya titik sampel
  ### R = jari-jari
  
  # Membangkitkan titik-titik acak di dalam kubus [-R, R]^3
  x <- runif(n_points, min = -R, max = R)
  y <- runif(n_points, min = -R, max = R)
  z <- runif(n_points, min = -R, max = R)
  
  # Menghitung jarak titik ke pusat (0, 0, 0) dan memeriksa apakah diterima
  in_sphere <- (x^2 + y^2 + z^2) <= R^2
  
  # Menghitung proporsi titik yang berada di dalam bola
  n_in_sphere <- sum(in_sphere)
  
  # Estimasi volume bola
  volume_cube <- (2 * R)^3
  volume_sphere_est <- (n_in_sphere / n_points) * volume_cube
  
  # Estimasi nilai π dari volume bola
  pi_estimate <- (3 / 4) * (volume_sphere_est / R^3)
  
  return(pi_estimate)
}
```

Simulasi:

```{r}
set.seed(123) # Untuk memastikan pengacakan konstan
n_points <- 1000000
pi_estimate <- estimate_pi(n_points)
cat("Estimasi nilai π:", pi_estimate, "\n")
```

Simulasi:

```{r}
set.seed(123) # Untuk memastikan pengacakan konstan

cat("Estimasi nilai π:", pi_estimate, "\n")

Nilai Jarak ke π
Simulasi 1000000: 3.144042|3.144042 − π| ≈ 0.00244935
Simulasi 10000000: 3.140233|3.140233 − π| ≈ 0.00135965

### 2.2. Simulasi Banyaknya Penjualan dengan *Empirical Probability*

```

Fungsi:

```{r}
simulasi.mc = function(x,y,n){
  ### Fungsi ini mensimulasikan banyaknya penjualan dengan metode Monte Carlo ###
  ### Input: 
  ### x = banyaknya permintaan
  ### y = frekuensi permintaan
  ### n = banyaknya hari
  
  # Menghitung pdf dan cdf banyaknya permintaan
  pdf = y/sum(y)
  cdf = cumsum(pdf)
  cdf[1] = pdf[1]
  for(i in 2:length(y)){
    cdf[i] = cdf[i-1] + pdf[i]
  }
  
  # Mencetak pdf dan cdf banyaknya permintaan
  tabel1 = data.frame(permintaan = x, freq = y, pdf, cdf)
  print(tabel1)
  
  # Mengacak bilangan sebanyak n
  set.seed(123)
  random = runif(n)
  cat("\n")
  cat("Nilai Random: ", round(random, 2), "\n")
  
  # Membandingkan bilangan random dengan interval bilangan
  kesimpulan = NULL
  cat("\n")
  for(i in 1:n){
    for(j in 1:length(x)){
      if(random[i] <= cdf[j]){
        kesimpulan[i] = x[j]
        break
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Mencetak tabel ramalan banyaknya permintaan
  tabel2 = data.frame(Hari = c(1:n), Ban = kesimpulan)
  print(tabel2)
}
```

Simulasi:

```{r}
set.seed(123)
permintaan = c("0", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5")
freq = c(10, 20, 40, 60, 40, 30)
n = 10
simulasi.mc(permintaan, freq, 10)
```

## 3. Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)

#### Kasus Markov Chain Diskrit

Fungsi:

```{r}
mcmc <- function(P, lambda, n1, n2, nama_states = NULL) {
  ### Fungsi ini mensimulasikan sampel Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) ###
  ### Input:
  ### P = matriks transisi
  ### lambda = distribusi awal
  ### n1 = periode burn-in
  ### n2 = jumlah sampel yang diinginkan
  ### nama_states = daftar nama untuk setiap state
  
  # Jika nama_states tidak diberikan, gunakan default 1, 2, ..., k
  if (!is.null(nama_states)) {
    states = nama_states
  } else {
    states = 1:length(lambda)
  }
  
  k = length(lambda)
  
  # Total sampel (termasuk burn-in)
  total_sampel = n1 + n2
  
  # Matriks untuk menyimpan hasil sampel
  x = numeric(total_sampel)
  
  # State awal (diambil dari distribusi awal lambda)
  x[1] = sample(1:k, 1, prob = lambda)  # Gunakan indeks 1 hingga k untuk sampling awal
  
  # Periode burn-in
  for (i in 2:n1) {
    x[i] = sample(1:k, 1, prob = P[x[i - 1], ])  # Transisi berdasarkan matriks P
  }
  
  # Periode pengambilan sampel setelah burn-in
  for (i in (n1 + 1):total_sampel) {
    x[i] = sample(1:k, 1, prob = P[x[i - 1], ])  # Transisi berdasarkan matriks P
  }
  
  # Mengambil sampel setelah periode burn-in
  sampel_akhir = x[(n1 + 1):total_sampel]
  
  # Mengubah indeks hasil sampling menjadi nama states
  sampel = states[sampel_akhir]
  
  return(sampel)
}
```

Simulasi:

```{r}
set.seed(123)
# Transition Matrix
P = matrix(c(0.9, 0.1, 0.2, 0.8), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)
# Initial State
lambda = c(0.50, 0.50)
# Number of burn-in period
n1 = 200
# Number of samples
n2 = 10000
# Name of state
states = c("Coke", "Pepsi")
# Simulate the MCMC
x = mcmc(P, lambda, n1, n2, nama_states = states)
head(x)
```

Eksplorasi hasil simulasi:

```{r}
# Menghitung probabilitas masing-masing state
prop.table(table(x))
```

#### Kasus Markov Chain Kontinu

*Sampling* distribusi yang... aneh?

Target:

```{r}
# Target distribution
target <- function(x) {
  return(exp(-x^2) * (2 + sin(5*x) + sin(2*x)))
}
```

Fungsi:

```{r}
mcmc_mh <- function(x, sigma) {
  proposed_x <- rnorm(1, mean = x, sd = sigma)
  accept_prob <- min(1, target(proposed_x) / target(x))
  u <- runif(1)
  if(u <= accept_prob) {
    value <- proposed_x
    accepted <- TRUE
  } else {
    value <- x
    accepted <- FALSE
  }
  out <- data.frame(value = value, accepted = accepted)
  out
}
```

Fungsi Simulasi:

```{r}
mcmc_mh_sampler <- function(initial_value, n = 1000, sigma = 1,
                            burnin = 0, lag = 1){
  results <- list()
  current_state <- initial_value
  for(i in 1:burnin) {
    out <- mcmc_mh(current_state, sigma)
    current_state <- out$value
  }
  for(i in 1:n) {
    for(j in 1:lag) {
      out <- mcmc_mh(current_state, sigma)
      current_state <- out$value
    }
    results[[i]] <- out
  }
  results <- do.call(rbind, results)
  results
}
```

Simulasi:

```{r}
set.seed(123)
out <- mcmc_mh_sampler(initial_value = 0, n = 10000, burnin = 100)
head(out)
```

Plot hasil dengan Line Plot:

```{r}
plot(out$value, type = "l", col = "blue", lwd = 2, xlab = "Iteration", ylab = "Value", main = "MCMC Metropolis-Hastings")
```

Plot hasil dengan Histogram:

```{r}
hist(out$value, breaks = 50, col = "lightblue", main = "Histogram of MCMC Metropolis-Hastings", xlab = "Value")
```

KDE plot:

```{r}
density <- density(out$value)
plot(density, main = "Density Plot of MCMC Metropolis-Hastings", xlab = "Value", ylab = "Density")
```

#### MCMC untuk Bayesian Regression

Inisiasi Data:

```{r}
set.seed(123)
# Simulated data
n <- 1000
x <- rnorm(n, 10, 5)
beta0_true <- 2
beta1_true <- 3
sigma_true <- 2
y <- beta0_true + beta1_true * x + rnorm(n, 0, sigma_true)
```

Pembentukan fungsi likelihood, log-prior, dan log-posterior:

```{r}
# Prior parameters
mu_0 <- 0
sd_0 <- 10
mu_1 <- 0
sd_1 <- 10
alpha_s2 <- 1
beta_s2 <- 1

# Likelihood function
likelihood <- function(y, x, beta0, beta1, sigma2) {
  n = length(y)
  ll = - n/2 * log(2*pi) - n/2 * log(sigma2) - 1/(2*sigma2) * sum((y - beta0 - beta1 * x)^2)
  return(ll)
}

# Prior function
log_prior <- function(beta0, beta1, sigma2) {
  # Normal prior for beta0 and beta1
  prior_beta0 <- dnorm(beta0, mu_0, sd_0, log = TRUE)
  prior_beta1 <- dnorm(beta1, mu_1, sd_1, log = TRUE)
  
  # Inverse-gamma prior for sigma2
  prior_sigma2 <- dgamma(1 / sigma2, alpha_s2, beta_s2, log = TRUE) - 2 * log(sigma2)
  
  return(prior_beta0 + prior_beta1 + prior_sigma2)
}

# Posterior function (log scale)
log_posterior <- function(beta0, beta1, sigma2, y, x) {
  log_prior(beta0, beta1, sigma2) + likelihood(y, x, beta0, beta1, sigma2)
}
```

Fungsi:

```{r}
mcmc_metropolis <- function(y, x, burnin, samplesize, initial_values, proposal_sd) {
  n <- length(y)
  total_samples <- burnin + samplesize
  beta0 <- rep(NA, total_samples)
  beta1 <- rep(NA, total_samples)
  sigma2 <- rep(NA, total_samples)
  acc_status <- rep(NA, total_samples)
  
  # Initial values
  beta0[1] <- initial_values[1]
  beta1[1] <- initial_values[2]
  sigma2[1] <- initial_values[3]
  
  for (i in 2:total_samples) {
    # Proposal
    beta0_prop <- rnorm(1, beta0[i - 1], proposal_sd[1])
    beta1_prop <- rnorm(1, beta1[i - 1], proposal_sd[2])
    sigma2_prop <- abs(rnorm(1, sigma2[i - 1], proposal_sd[3]))  # Ensure sigma2 > 0
    
    # Acceptance probability
    log_alpha <- log_posterior(beta0_prop, beta1_prop, sigma2_prop, y, x) - 
      log_posterior(beta0[i - 1], beta1[i - 1], sigma2[i - 1], y, x)
    
    # Accept or reject
    if (log(runif(1)) < min(log_alpha, 1)) {
      beta0[i] <- beta0_prop
      beta1[i] <- beta1_prop
      sigma2[i] <- sigma2_prop
      acc_status[i] <- TRUE
    } else {
      beta0[i] <- beta0[i - 1]
      beta1[i] <- beta1[i - 1]
      sigma2[i] <- sigma2[i - 1]
      acc_status[i] <- FALSE
    }
  }
  
  out <- data.frame(beta0 = beta0[(burnin + 1):total_samples],
                    beta1 = beta1[(burnin + 1):total_samples],
                    sigma2 = sigma2[(burnin + 1):total_samples],
                    acc_status = acc_status[(burnin + 1):total_samples])
  return(out)
}
```

Simulasi:

```{r}
set.seed(123)
burnin <- 1000  # Burn-in period
samplesize <- 5000  # Number of samples to draw
initial_values <- c(1, 1, 1)  # Initial values for beta0, beta1, sigma2
proposal_sd <- c(0.05, 0.05, 0.05)  # Proposal standard deviations

out <- mcmc_metropolis(y, x, burnin, samplesize, initial_values, proposal_sd)
head(out)
```

Plot hasil:

```{r}
# Plot trace
par(mfrow = c(3, 1))
plot(out$beta0, type = "l", col = "blue", lwd = 2, xlab = "Iteration", ylab = "Value", main = "Trace of beta0")
plot(out$beta1, type = "l", col = "blue", lwd = 2, xlab = "Iteration", ylab = "Value", main = "Trace of beta1")
plot(out$sigma2, type = "l", col = "blue", lwd = 2, xlab = "Iteration", ylab = "Value", main = "Trace of sigma2")
```

Estimasi:

```{r}
# Posterior means
posterior_means <- colMeans(out[, 1:3])
posterior_means
```

```{r}
summary(lm(y ~ x))
```
